title: Stone and brick materials: rock, cobblestone, bricks, stone blocks, roofs, plaster
summary: 11 tiling 1K PBR masonry materials: rock, cobblestone, brick_red, brick_old, stone_blocks, stone_wall_mossy, roof_slate, roof_terracotta, plaster, limestone, slate; triplanar + UV versions.
use_when: Buildings, castles, dungeons, walls, streets, roofs, cliffs or ruins should look like real masonry instead of grey boxes.
how_to_use: Assign with mesh_instance.material_override = load("res://starter/mat-stone-brick/<name>_triplanar.tres") (or CSGShape3D.material = ...). _triplanar files map in world space at real-world scale with no UVs: use them for level geometry, CSG, BoxMesh/PlaneMesh floors and walls, terrain chunks; pieces placed side by side tile seamlessly. Do not use _triplanar on moving or animated objects (the texture slides); use <name>.tres there and set uv1_scale to mesh size in metres divided by the repeat size. To tint, duplicate the material and set albedo_color. Roofs: use roof_slate.tres / roof_terracotta.tres (UV versions) on a PrismMesh; at uv1_scale (1,1,1) a 1.6 x 1.0 x 1.4 m prism shows correctly sized tiles running down the slope (scale uv1_scale up for bigger roofs). Brick and stone_wall rows run horizontally on vertical faces. For a real-geometry 3D cobble street use the mat-cobble-paving pack instead of the flat cobblestone texture.
